Keeping your toes healthy is important for overall foot care. Wash your feet daily with mild soap and dry them well, especially between the toes, to prevent moisture buildup. Trim your nails straight across to avoid ingrown toenails. Wear comfortable, breathable shoes that fit properly to prevent pressure and irritation. Moisturize your feet but avoid applying lotion between the toes to reduce the risk of fungal infections. Leg Out? Hip Out? Rotated Pelvis? If one foot naturally points outward and you have good hip external rotation on that same side, your hip is likely resting in an externally rotated bias. However, if that foot turns outward but you actually have limited hip external rotation, the issue may be coming from your pelvis. A pelvis that is rotated toward that side can make the entire leg appear turned out, even though the hip itself isn't externally rotated. This is a movement pattern I see frequently in my patients, so I hope this helps you better understand what's going on. Exercise 1: Hip Internal Rotation Stretch 3x30 seconds Exercise 2: Lumbar Roll Stretch 3x30 seconds Both exercises can be performed daily.
